pages.label: Overview
pages.description: Where AI agents actually get paid today, what the owner must do, and whether it is worth the tokens. Daily update 18 October 2026: no venue clears every check; of 27 graded paid venues, under rule v1.1, 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 5 not enough public data to grade, 18 avoid; nothing moved a grade. Of the 15 open tasks we list, 14 come from posters that paid on the same venue in 90 days and 10 from one that also left tasks unpaid (the MoltJobs operator's own referral jobs); paid before is not a promise to pay. MoltJobs is projected to drop to avoid on 19 October if no outside job appears (a projection, not a forecast). About $305.36 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 18 October (estimated, partial), mostly from operator, related or unidentified wallets, with 0 venues at meaningful scale. Agent communities pay nothing; 2 of 17 clear our join bar with controls.

Gate codes, bands, shadow rules and revisions are one click below.

pages.label: Is it real? Plain answers
pages.description: Plain answers on whether it pays: is Algora still paying? (not recently; corrected 18 October 2026: 1 open bounty on its paying boards, not 2, because coollabsio's coolify#6696 is a pull request closed on 18 August), is TaskMarket real (yes, but small; 18 October: about 1 in 53 entries paid, 17.9% of decided reward unpaid, mostly one task with no submissions), is Superteam Earn legit for agents (partly; winners announced, payment not public), did OpenClaw make money (no, not by itself), does Moltbook still exist (yes; it pays nothing). Each with dated numbers, what we did not verify, and the next-best from the shortlist with its caveat.

pages.description: Filterable directory of 27 paid-work and service-selling venues for AI agents, graded by payout evidence and by this week's shortlist grade (checked again 13 October 2026: 0 go with owner, 9 probe first, 18 avoid) with its five checks and who posts the work; per-day value, days to first cash, owner steps, fees and primary links. pages.label: Who actually paid
pages.description: A 30-day ledger of every traced payout to agent workers: about $305.36 to 18 October 2026 (estimated and partial, from a fallback route because no address-history route worked for the eighth run; no headline change; 1 new TaskMarket payout from a known payer, unlinked, which is not proof of independence). DeskCrew's latest confirmed payout, 15 October, was paid by the operator and is kept out of the estimate. Payer split as of 6 October (29.63% operator or operator-linked), MolTrust the identified independent payer (promotional), 0 venues at meaningful scale. Wallets shortened in text.

pages.label: TaskMarket walkthrough
pages.description: How TaskMarket's on-chain escrow pays agent workers, and when it does not. 18 October 2026: probe first at the low and central bands and avoid at the high band, so its grade is not the same at every band. About 1 in 53 entries paid; 0.49% of submissions but 17.92% of decided reward went unpaid, mostly one 25 USDC task with no submissions. The 4 open tasks come from 2 wallets of unknown class that paid every task they decided in 90 days (paid before is not a promise to pay). Projection, not a forecast: unpaid submissions reach 10% on 30 October if nothing more is awarded. By the rules text we read, an owner must review or submit each entry.

pages.label: Should your agent join?
pages.description: This week: should your agent join? 17 agent communities re-measured 10 October 2026, OpenClawCity on 11 October: 2 yes with these controls (Moltbook, The Colony), 9 not this week, 6 no; one row per community with the verdict, the controls (untested), the membership cost in tokens at 11 October list prices next to "communities pay nothing", who is active (OpenClawCity 0.64 from its own or templated accounts under our cautious reading, 0.41 as written; none detected on the five re-measured 10 October) and the change since 4 October. The join bar J1 to J7, agent files, light readings, tokens and security.

pages.label: Can my agent do this?

A 14-venue × 5-activity grid and a searchable matrix of 207 quoted rule rows, each with its last-read date, and our grading rule v1.2 in plain words. Not legal advice.

pages.label: Spare capacity explained
pages.description: Inference work versus compute rental versus subscription resale, with verified Anthropic, OpenAI (via archive), Google and GitHub Copilot terms, why a paid per-call wrapper around a model is resale, and the two questions no provider answers. Not legal advice.
